assumptions: Each fortnight to 31 March: last fortnight's crush × the median path of past seasons from the same date (MAPA, 2014/15 on).
Adjusted by rain: estimated stoppage days in that fortnight above or below the 2011–2025 normal for the same dates reduce or add to the crush, at the rate seen in past fortnights.

Stoppage days: observed to the latest ERA5 day, then the ensemble forecast (10th / 50th / 90th percentile member for dry / base / wet), then 2011–2025 climatology to 31 December (20th / 50th / 80th percentile); January–March at normal.
Sugar per tonne of the remaining cane = last fortnight's kg/t × the median ratio of later-season to same-fortnight kg/t in past seasons (mix and ATR both fall late in the season).
Mills' end dates follow past seasons; if more mills stop early than usual the outcome falls below the wet case.

next_season.text: No 2027/28 production view yet: the first public read is ISMA's satellite cane-area assessment (usually July) and the monsoon. What is known: if only the unused part of the duty-free quota (about 7.4 lakh t) arrives this season, India starts 2027/28 with about 22 lakh t (0.9 months of consumption), so any shortfall in the 2027/28 crop goes straight to imports.

imports.most_likely: Most likely: about 9 lakh t of imports in 2026/27 (ISMA crop, normal 2027 monsoon, No. 11 at 18.34¢): about 3 lakh t more under the duty-free quota by 31 March, about 5 more if the quota is extended again (it has been twice) and about 2 beyond the 10 lakh t only if summer prices rise to the level that opened the quota (about Rs 5,800/qtl). On the desk's lower mid crop, about 18 lakh t. Range across monsoon cases for the ISMA and desk-mid crops: 4 to 30 lakh t. Reaching the 2.5-month norm would need 35 lakh t (44 on the desk mid crop), which the market is not paying for.

implied.read: Domestic ex-mill (Maharashtra S/30) is Rs 4,950/qtl, flat over four weeks (-1.8%) and Rs 1,325 below the 2026-08 peak; it sits Rs 1,221/qtl over landed raws at zero duty, not enough to cover freight, refining and margin, so TRQ imports pay only with No. 11 below about 17.7¢ (current 18.34¢). With 2.6 of 10 lakh t of the quota used by 2026-10-19 and part of it re-offered, the market is pricing a gap that the quota and a stock run-down can cover, not a 50 lakh t shortage. If only the likely TRQ tonnage arrives, ISMA's crop and 278 lakh t of consumption end September 2027 at about 26 lakh t (1.1 months): tight, so the test comes in June–September, when the crush is over and prices, not the balance, decide whether the quota is widened.

items.detail: Federal tax on gasoline cut by R$0.63/l (total federal tax left R$0.16/l); hydrous ethanol PIS/Cofins zeroed (R$0.19/l). Replaced a R$0.44/l gasoline subsidy that ended 9 Sep.
items.effect_on_ethanol_parity: Lower gasoline pump price caps what hydrous can charge at the pump (70% rule); the ethanol tax cut offsets part of it

items.detail: Gasoline federal tax cut raised from R$0.63 to R$0.89/l (PIS/Pasep, Cofins and Cide at zero); hydrous ethanol tax cut kept at R$0.19/l; subsidy to ethanol producers raised from R$0.25 to R$0.43/l.
items.effect_on_ethanol_parity: The producer subsidy adds to mill ethanol revenue: about 2¢/lb sugar-equivalent at R$0.43/l

items.detail: PIS/Pasep and Cofins stay at zero on gasoline (Cide also zero) and on hydrous ethanol; extraordinary subsidy of R$0.428 per litre of hydrous ethanol to producers and co-operatives, to 9 December 2026.
items.effect_on_ethanol_parity: Lapse on 9 Dec would lift gasoline by the R$0.89/l of tax and take the R$0.428/l subsidy away from mills: watch for a further extension
